messages:
maria (support): FYI incoming from ACME — their rerank calls started failing around 09:12 UTC with a model-related error. They say scores are all 0 and responses are 410/ModelDeprecated.

jane (acme-customer): Confirmed. Our logs show repeated requests to /v1/rerank with model "ranker-v1" and we started getting: 

```
HTTP/1.1 410 Gone
Content-Type: application/json
{
  \"error\": {\"type\": \"ModelDeprecated\", \"message\": \"model 'ranker-v1' has been retired\"},
  \"warning\": \"use alias 'latest-ranker' or model 'ranker-v2'\"
}
```

jane (acme-customer): Repro (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/rerank \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXXX\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{"model":"ranker-v1","queries":["q1","q2"],"candidates":[...] }'
```

maria (support): Can you paste the full request body? curious if they're hitting an alias or hard id. Also any client logs that show cached model id?

jane (acme-customer): They pinned the model id in their config (hard-coded). SDK was initialised months ago; they haven't redeployed the service since the deprecation.

ben (eng): That explains it — ranker-v1 was removed in the last cleanup. We expose an alias 'latest-ranker' that points to ranker-v2. The API will return a deprecation 410 for retired model ids. If the client uses the alias (or the v2 id) the calls succeed.

ben (eng): Quick repro on our side: same curl but model "ranker-v2" or "latest-ranker" returns 200 with expected scores. The issue is client-side pinning/caching.

arnold (sre): Two operational notes: 1) We do include an HTTP header when we return deprecation that hints the replacement: `X-Model-Deprecation: retry-with-alias=latest-ranker` 2) Some SDKs cache resolver entries for 24h — restarting the process or clearing SDK cache forces re-resolve.

maria (support): Customer says they can't do a full deploy this week, need a short-term mitigation. Can we temporarily re-enable ranker-v1 or add a redirect mapping ranker-v1 -> ranker-v2?

ben (eng): We could create a control-plane compatibility mapping so calls referencing ranker-v1 are routed to ranker-v2 for a short window. That carries risk (behavioral differences) but is doable. Need approvals (PM + infra) and an entry in the change log.

arnold (sre): If we do that, we should: 1) add a notice in logs so customers are aware 2) rate-limit the fallback to catch edge cases 3) schedule a rollback window. Otherwise we may mask bugs.

maria (support): I told the customer the safest path is to update to alias 'latest-ranker' or model 'ranker-v2' and to restart their service to bust SDK cache. Sent them exact steps to clear cache: 
```
# node SDK
rm -rf ~/.redwood/cache/alias.json && pm2 restart all
# or restart container service
```

maria (support): Also sent them this note: if you see `X-Model-Deprecation` header, switch to the alias indicated.

support-bot: Ticket INC-4321 created and linked to this thread.

docs-bot: Suggestion queued: add a docs section on deprecation headers and SDK cache behavior (PR required).

ben (eng): I'll draft a short-term compatibility mapping RFC and post in #eng-runtime. If customer still needs immediate access after that we can consider enabling the mapping for 48h. Otherwise strongly recommend client update.

maria (support): Customer accepted the temporary compatibility mapping as a last resort. I'll coordinate approvals.

jane (acme-customer): Thanks — we'll try an immediate restart and point to alias. If that fails we'll request the temporary mapping.

ben (eng): Recap actions: 1) maria to get customer logs + confirm SDK version 2) if customer can't update, maria to request compatibility mapping with SRE + PM approval 3) arnold to prepare rollout/rollback plan 4) docs-bot to create docs PR

maria (support): Got it. I'll update this thread with customer confirmation and the ticket ID. :thumbsup:
